h.strategy: After listing and negating default assumptions, keep only the negations that a general mechanism supports. Candidate mechanisms: parent quality (strong parents leave little room to improve and have more to lose), redundancy (duplicate or similar options dilute each other's contribution), and bottlenecks (an option matters little when it is not on the path to the output, however strong it is). Prefer predictions in which a usually helpful edit becomes neutral or harmful in a common context, or a usually harmful edit becomes harmless. Avoid conditions that only a few parents satisfy. Spread hypotheses across different edited fields and condition fields. Give at least four 'lower' predictions where the intuitive guess would be 'higher'.

hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 receives no input, so a conv on edge 2 is off the live path (bottleneck) and adds nothing.
Node 1 is dead when edge 0 is none, so a stronger op on edge 4 carries no signal.
Replacing none with a conv on the direct input-to-output path adds a whole new path, which gives more gain than upgrading an existing op.
A skip already supplies a clean direct path, so replacing it with a conv gains less (redundancy) than filling an empty edge.
Upgrading 1x1 to 3x3 is a smaller step than replacing a weak op such as none or pooling, so the gain is lower.
A strong direct conv path to the output already exists, so another conv feeding the output is partly redundant and the parent has less room to improve.
With edge 5 removed, node 2 only reaches the output through nothing, so edge 1 is off the output path and its upgrade is wasted.
With edge 4 gone, node 1 can only reach the output through edge 2 and edge 5, so edge 0's upgrade passes through fewer paths.
Removing edge 4 costs little when a strong direct conv on edge 3 already feeds the output (redundancy), so the drop is smaller.
Replacing a strong conv with pooling loses far more than replacing a weak op, so the edit is much more harmful.
